title: loadng: unwrap() calls lack infallibility documentation
description:
Several .unwrap() calls in from_bytes() rely on implicit length guarantees:
- Line 479: sig_data.try_into().unwrap() - safe because match arm guarantees len==48
- Lines 487-488: data[4..20].try_into().unwrap() - safe because line 470 checks len>=36
- Lines 560, 569-570: same pattern in Rrep::from_bytes()
- Lines 671, 675: same pattern in Rerr::from_bytes()

While the logic is sound (parent length checks guarantee slice sizes), the infallibility reasoning is implicit. Security-critical parsing code should document why panics are unreachable. A future refactor could inadvertently break the invariant.

Suggestion: Add inline comments or use .expect() with the invariant stated, e.g.:
  data[4..20].try_into().expect("len checked at line 470")

Severity: P2 - correctness is fine but clarity aids security review.
